paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the One who made the world by wisdom is the One you can trust with your life. The speaker says, "Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding" (Proverbs 3:5). And he doesn't stop at trusting. He says to acknowledge the LORD in all your ways, and "He will make your paths straight" (Proverbs 3:6).

That's why the speaker can ask for the hard stuff too, like honoring the LORD with your wealth (Proverbs 3:9) and not rejecting His discipline (Proverbs 3:11). It's not easy, and I think some of it stings. But the reason is right there: "the LORD disciplines the one He loves, as does a father the son in whom he delights" (Proverbs 3:12). So a correction from Him isn't a door slamming. It's a Father who is holding on to you.

And then wisdom herself gets the spotlight. She is "more profitable than silver," and "nothing you desire compares with her" (Proverbs 3:14-15). She is "a tree of life to those who embrace her" (Proverbs 3:18). So go ahead and lean in, baker, because the same wisdom the LORD used to found the earth and establish the heavens is the wisdom He offers you (Proverbs 3:19-20).
